#### ****What’s in a game? Find out from the ESRB Rating System.****

The [Entertainment Software Rating Board](https://www.esrb.org/) (ESRB) is the non-profit, self-regulatory body for the video game industry. Established in 1994, ESRB assigns age and content rating information for video games and apps to help parents and caregivers decide which are appropriate for their family.

The ESRB [Advertising Review Council](https://www.esrb.org/ratings/principles-guidelines/) (ARC) enforces industry-adopted advertising guidelines, and the [Privacy Certified](https://www.esrb.org/privacy/) program helps members ensure responsible online and mobile privacy practices.

**The ESRB rating system in a nutshell →**

* **Rating categories**Suggest age appropriateness (such as “T” for youth ages 13 and up).
* **Content descriptors**Indicate content that may have prompted a particular rating (such as violence, alcohol references or crude humor).
* **Interactive elements**Highlight a game’s interactive or online features (such as users’ ability to communicate with other users or to make in-game purchases).

# Understanding video games age ratings

Every parent wants their children to be safe online, but how do you know if the video games that they’re playing are age appropriate?

Most games contain an age rating on either its packaging or online, and this rating will differ depending on where the game was released. In the United States, Canada and Mexico, the ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board) system is used to help distinguish what games are suitable for different ages and in the UK and most European countries the PEGI (Pan European Games Information) system is used.

These age ratings help consumers to decide whether a game is suitable for the intended user and ensures children are not exposed to inappropriate content. The ratings should not be misinterpreted as to who will enjoy the game or how difficult the game is, it should only be used as an age rating.

But what do the various video games age ratings mean?

## ESRB system - United States, Mexico and Canada

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| EC | Early Childhood. Suitable for children aged 3 or older, there will be no inappropriate content. E.g. Dora the Explorer, Dragon Tales. |
| E | Suitable for all age groups. The game should not contain any sounds or images likely to scare young children. No bad language should be used. E.g. Just Dance, FIFA. |
| E 10+ | Suitable for those aged 10 or above. There could be mild forms of violence, and some scenes might be frightening for children. E.g. Minecraft Dungeons, Plants vs Zombies. |
| T | Suitable for those aged 13 or above. The game could feature more realistic and graphic scenes of violence. E.g. Fortnite, Sims 4. |
| M | Suitable for those aged 17 or above. This rating is used when the violence becomes realistic and would be expected in real life. Bad language, and the use of tobacco, alcohol or illegal drugs can also be present. E.g. Ark: Survival Evolved, Destiny 2. |
| AO | Suitable for adults aged 18 or above. The adult classification is used when there are extreme levels of violence and motiveless killing. Glamorisation of drugs, gambling and sexual activity can also be featured. E.g. Grand Theft Auto V, Fallout 4. |
| RP | Rating Pending. Titles with the RP rating have not yet been assigned a final ESRB rating. |

The age ratings are also accompanied by descriptors that show what the content of a video game may contain, e.g. bad language, fear and violence.

## PEGI system - United Kingdom and most European countries

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| PEGI 3 | Suitable for all age groups. The game should not contain any sounds or images likely to scare young children. No bad language should be used. E.g. Just Dance, FIFA. |
| PEGI 7 | Suitable for those aged 7 or above. There could be mild forms of violence, and some scenes might be frightening for children. E.g. Minecraft Dungeons, Plants vs Zombies. |
| PEGI 12 | Suitable for those aged 12 or above. The game could feature more realistic and graphic scenes of violence. E.g. Fortnite, Sims 4. |
| PEGI 16 | Suitable for those aged 16 or above. This rating is used when the violence becomes realistic and would be expected in real life. Bad language, and the use of tobacco, alcohol or illegal drugs can also be present. E.g. Ark: Survival Evolved, Destiny 2. |
| PEGI 18 | Suitable for those aged 18 or above. The adult classification is used when there are extreme levels of violence and motiveless killing. Glamorisation of drugs, gambling and sexual activity can also be featured. E.g. Grand Theft Auto V, Fallout 4. |

The age ratings are also accompanied by PEGI descriptors that show what the content of a video game may contain, e.g. bad language, fear and violence.

We would suggest that before you purchase a game to check the ESRB or PEGI age rating and the content descriptors, as these will provide good guidance on whether a game is suitable for your child. Following the games age ratings will ensure that children only play games that are suitable for their age group, and that they are not exposed to inappropriate content or language. Another way to stay informed about the game’s children are playing is to [set up parental controls](/en/blog/mobile-lifestyle/how-to-setup-parental-controls-on-your-pc-or-mac). Taking advantage of both these options will keep children safe while playing video games.

results.content:
The Pan European Game Information (PEGI) is a European video game content rating system established to help European parents make informed decisions on buying computer games with logos on games boxes. It was developed by the Interactive Software Federation of Europe (now Video Games Europe")) and came into use in April 2003; it replaced many national age rating systems with a single European system. The PEGI system is now used in more than thirty-one countries and is based on a code of conduct, [...] Games are classified by the Council of Cinematographic Classification (Consejo de Calificación Cinematográfica) which is a central agency under the Ministry of Education.

The current age ratings are:

 ER (Especialmente Recomendado) – Recommended for children.
 TE (Toda Edad) – All ages.
 8+ – Not recommended for children under 8 years of age.
 14+ – Not recommended for children under 14 years of age.
 18+ – Not recommended for children under 18 years of age. [...] over 13 years of age" and "Suitable for those over 18 years of age". In practice, this system has never been enforced or put in active use. Storefronts and retailers choose to use the ESRB, instead.

An example of different rating systems on video game discs which is common practice in Europe and Australia. From top left to down right: [the Russian video game rating system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Protecting_Children_from_Information_Harmful_to_Their_Health_and_Development "On Protecting Children from Information Harmful to Their Health and Development"), the European [PEGI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEGI "PEGI") system, the German [USK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USK "USK"), all sharing the same age classification on this example game.

A **video game content rating system** is a [system used for the classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_rating "Content rating") of [video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") based on suitability for target audiences. Most of these systems are associated with and/or sponsored by a government, and are sometimes part of the local [motion picture rating system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_picture_rating_system "Motion picture rating system"). The utility of such ratings has been called into question by studies that publish findings, such as 90% of teenagers claim that their parents "never" check the ratings before allowing them to rent or buy video games,[[1]](#cite_note-1) and as such, calls have been made to "fix" the existing rating systems.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) Video game content rating systems can be used as the basis for laws that cover the sales of video games to minors, such as in Australia. Rating checking and approval is part of the [game localization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_localization "Game localization") when they are being prepared for their distribution in other countries or locales. These rating systems have also been used to voluntarily restrict sales of certain video games by stores, such as the German retailer Galeria Kaufhof's removal of all video games rated 18+ by the USK following the [Winnenden school shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnenden_school_shooting "Winnenden school shooting").[[4]](#cite_note-4)

## Initial controversy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Video_game_content_rating_system&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Initial controversy")]

Main article: [Video game controversies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_controversies "Video game controversies")

Similar to other forms of media, [video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") have been the subject of argument between leading professionals and restriction and prohibition. Often these bouts of criticism come from use of debated topics such as video game [graphic violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphic_violence "Graphic violence"), virtual sex, violent and gory scenes, partial or full nudity, drug use, portrayal of [criminal behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime "Crime") or other provocative and objectionable material. Video games have also been studied for links to [addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_addiction "Video game addiction") and [aggression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggression "Aggression"). A meta analysis of studies from both eastern and western countries yielded evidence that "strongly suggests that exposure to violent video games is a causal risk factor for increased aggressive behavior, aggressive cognition, and aggressive affect and for decreased empathy and prosocial behavior."[[12]](#cite_note-12)

There are also groups that have argued to the contrary, that few if any scientifically proven studies exist to back up these claims, and that the [video game industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_industry "Video game industry") has become an easy target for the media to blame for many contemporary issues.[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) Researchers have also proposed potential positive effects of video games on aspects of social and cognitive development and psychological well-being.[[16]](#cite_note-16) It has been shown that action video game players have better [hand-eye coordination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand-eye_coordination "Hand-eye coordination") and visuo-motor skills, such as their resistance to distraction, their sensitivity to information in the peripheral vision and their ability to count briefly presented objects, than non-players.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

### Argentina

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Video_game_content_rating_system&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Argentina")]

The law 26.043 (passed in 2005) states that the **National Council of Children, Youth and Family** ('**Consejo Nacional de la Niñez, Adolescencia y la Familia'**) in coordination with the **[National Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Cinema_and_Audiovisual_Arts "National Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual Arts")** will be the [government agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_agency "Government agency") that assigns age ratings.[[18]](#cite_note-18)[[19]](#cite_note-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20) The Argentine Game Developer Association (***Asociación de Desarrolladores de Videojuegos Argentina***) was critical of the law.[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22)[[23]](#cite_note-23) There are three ratings: "Suitable for all public", "Suitable for those over 13 years of age" and "Suitable for those over 18 years of age".[[24]](#cite_note-24) In practice, this system has never been enforced or put in active use. Storefronts and retailers choose to use the ESRB, instead.[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26)

* Advisory categories
  + General (**G**) – *General*. The content is very mild in impact. The G classification is suitable for everyone.
  + Parental Guidance (**PG**) – *Parental guidance recommended*. The content is mild in impact. It is not recommended for viewing or playing by persons under 15 without guidance from parents or guardians.
  + Mature (**M**) – *Recommended for mature audiences*. The content is moderate in impact. Children under 15 may legally access this material because it is an advisory category. However, M classified films and computer games may include classifiable elements such as violence and nudity of moderate impact that are not recommended for children under 15 years.
* Restricted categories
  + Mature Accompanied (**MA 15+**) – *Not suitable for people under 15. Under 15s must be accompanied by a parent or adult guardian*. The content is strong in impact.
  + Restricted (**R 18+**) – *Restricted to 18 years and over*. The content is high in impact. Despite this category being legally restricted, in Queensland the restriction is not applicable to persons under 2.

The **Australian Classification Board** (**ACB**) is a [statutory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute "Statute") classification body formed by the [Australian Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Australia "Government of Australia") which classifies [films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film "Film"), [video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") and [publications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publication "Publication") for exhibition, sale or hire in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia") since its establishment in 1970. The Classification Board was originally incorporated in the **Office of Film and Literature Classification** (**OFLC**) which was dissolved in 2006. Originally a part of the [Attorney-General's Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney-General's_Department_(Australia) "Attorney-General's Department (Australia)") and overseen by the [Minister for Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_for_Justice_(Australia) "Minister for Justice (Australia)"), the ACB is now a branch of the [Department of Communications and the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Communications_and_the_Arts "Department of Communications and the Arts") which provides administrative support to the Board and is overseen by the [Minister for Communications & the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_for_Communications_(Australia) "Minister for Communications (Australia)"). Decisions made by the Board may be reviewed by the Australian [Classification Review Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Classification_Review_Board "Australian Classification Review Board").

It was developed by the Interactive Software Federation of Europe (now [Video Games Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_Games_Europe?action=edit&redlink=1 "Video Games Europe (page does not exist)"))[[30]](#cite_note-30) and came into use in April 2003; it replaced many national age rating systems with a single European system. The PEGI system is now used in more than thirty-one countries and is based on a code of conduct, a set of rules to which every publisher using the PEGI system is contractually committed. PEGI self-regulation is composed by five age categories and seven content descriptors that advise the suitability and content of a game for a certain age range based on the games content. The ratings are:

* **3**: Suitable for all age groups.
* **7**: Not suitable for younger children.
* **12**: Not suitable for persons under 12 years of age.
* **16**: Not suitable for persons under 16 years of age.
* **18**: For adults.

The ratings do not indicate the difficulty of the game or the skill required to play it.[[5]](#cite_note-auto-5)

Main article: [Bureau of Indian Standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Indian_Standards "Bureau of Indian Standards")

On 10 March 2026, the [Bureau of Indian Standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Indian_Standards "Bureau of Indian Standards") (BIS), under the Media and Entertainment Services Sectional Committee (SSD 13), notified **IS 19690:2026** (*Video and Digital Games – Age Rating and Content Descriptor Labels – Specification*), establishing India's first national age-rating and content descriptor framework for video and digital games.[[31]](#cite_note-Exchange4Media2026-31) Prior to this, India lacked a standardized domestic video game rating system, relying instead on foreign systems like [PEGI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEGI "PEGI") or [ESRB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Software_Rating_Board "Entertainment Software Rating Board") on global distribution platforms.[[32]](#cite_note-OutlookIndia2026-32)

The standard defines a self-assessment model comprising six age categories aligned with Indian cinematic and OTT classification conventions:

* **U/A 0+**: Content suitable for all ages.
* **U/A 3+**: Content suitable for young children; minimal mature elements.
* **U/A 7+**: Content suitable for older children.
* **U/A 13+**: Content suitable for teenagers; mild violence or mature themes.
* **U/A 16+**: Content suitable for older teenagers; moderate violence, language, or mature themes.
* **A**: Adult content; explicit material or graphic violence.

The system also incorporates Content Descriptor Labels (CDLs) for elements such as violence, nudity, language, in-game purchases, and "socially sensitive themes" (covering cultural, religious, and community-related sensitivity).[[33]](#cite_note-LawAsia2026-33)

As of 2026, compliance with IS 19690:2026 remains voluntary. Neither a Quality Control Order (QCO) from the government nor a mandatory notification from the [Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Electronics_and_Information_Technology "Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology") (MeitY) has been issued to tie game distribution rights to obtaining a BIS classification.[[32]](#cite_note-OutlookIndia2026-32)[[33]](#cite_note-LawAsia2026-33)

Main article: [Indonesia Game Rating System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia_Game_Rating_System "Indonesia Game Rating System")

The **Indonesia Game Rating System** (**IGRS**) is the official video game content rating system founded and set by the Indonesian [Ministry of Communication and Informatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Communication_and_Informatics_(Indonesia) "Ministry of Communication and Informatics (Indonesia)") in 2016.[[34]](#cite_note-34) IGRS rates games that are developed and published in Indonesia. There are 5 classifications of ratings based on the game content, which includes the use of alcohol, cigarettes, drugs, violence, blood, language, sexual content, etc.

These are the following classifications:[[35]](#cite_note-35)

* **3+**  – Age 3 and over. No restricted content is shown including adult content, use of drugs, gambling simulation, and online interactions.
* **7+**  – Age 7 and over. No restricted content is shown including adult content, use of drugs, gambling simulation, and online interactions.
* **13+**  – Age 13 and over. Restricted contents are partially shown, including light use of drugs and alcohol by figures/background characters, cartoon violence, mild language, gambling simulation, horror theme, and online interactions.
* **15+**  – Age 15 and over. Restricted contents are partially shown, including limited animated violence without hatred, online interactions with language filters, blood elements, and non-sexual adult humor.
* **18+**  – Age 18 and over. Restricted contents are mostly shown, if not all, including use of drugs and alcohol by main characters, realistic violence (blood, gore, mutilation, etc.), crude humor, gambling simulation, horror theme, and online interactions.

Since November 2019, various imported [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation "PlayStation") titles released since then have been rated by the IGRS after [SIE Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment") opened their Indonesian office. Those titles are also marked as "Official Indonesia Products" ([Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language "Indonesian language"): *Produk Resmi Indonesia*).

In 2024, the Ministry of Communications and Informatics revised the IGRS in Ministerial Regulation MCI 2/2024, subsequently requiring that every [video game publisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_publisher "Video game publisher") to have an Indonesian representative office, as all games imported into the country must be age rated. After overhauling and launching the new application system in October 2025, this will be enforced in practise starting January 2026.

### Japan

In Japan, the content rating is not required by law, but most commercial video game publishers take the industry self-regulations. Console manufacturers often require video game publishers to have their games rated by CERO. Distributors of [PC games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer_game "Personal computer game") (mostly [dating sims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dating_sim "Dating sim"), [visual novels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_novel "Visual novel"), and [eroge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eroge "Eroge")) require games having the approval of EOCS or Japan contents Review Center.[[38]](#cite_note-38) These ratings are referred to by local governments, and the Ordinance Regarding the Healthy Development of Youths ([青少年健全育成条例](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/青少年保護育成条例 "ja:青少年保護育成条例")) prohibits retailers from supplying 18+ rating games to persons under 18.[[39]](#cite_note-39)[[40]](#cite_note-40) [Dōjin softs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dōjin_soft "Dōjin soft") do not have such restrictions, but distribution of obscene materials can be punished under the [Article 175 of the Penal Code of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship_in_Japan "Censorship in Japan").

The **Office of Film and Literature Classification** (**OFLC**) is the government agency in [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand") that is responsible for [classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship "Censorship") of all [films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film "Film"), [videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videotape "Videotape"), [publications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publications "Publications"), and some [video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") in New Zealand. It was created by the [Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Films,_Videos,_and_Publications_Classification_Act_1993 "Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993") (FVPC Act), replacing various film classification acts, and is an independent [Crown entity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_entity "Crown entity")[[47]](#cite_note-47) in terms of the [Crown Entities Act 2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Entities_Act_2004 "Crown Entities Act 2004"). The head of the OFLC is called the Chief Censor, maintaining a title that has described the government officer in charge of [censorship in New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship_in_New_Zealand "Censorship in New Zealand") since 1916.

* **G**: This can be shown and sold to anyone.
* **PG**: Films and games with a PG label can be sold, hired, or shown to anyone. The PG label means guidance from a parent or guardian is recommended for younger viewers.
* **M**: Films and games with an M label can be sold, hired, or shown to anyone. Films with an M label are more suitable for mature audiences 16 years and over.[[48]](#cite_note-literature-48)
* **R13**: Restricted to persons 13 years and over.
* **R15**: Restricted to persons 15 years and over.
* **R16**: Restricted to persons 16 years and over.
* **R18**: Restricted to persons 18 years and over.
* **R**: Restricted to a particular class of people.

In December 2022, the federal government has announced plans to establish a dedicated regulation procedure and age rating specifically for digital products, which include video games. ### Vietnam

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Video_game_content_rating_system&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Vietnam")]

Video games in [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam") are classified by age ratings regulated by the government as part of the country's game licensing and content-classification framework. The system is administered by the **Authority of Broadcasting and Electronic Information** (ABEI) under the **[Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture,_Sports_and_Tourism_(Vietnam) "Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (Vietnam)")** ([Vietnamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamese_language "Vietnamese language"): *Bộ Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch*) (MOCST).[[72]](#cite_note-72) Prior to the government restructuring that took effect on 1 March 2025 under Decree No. 55/2025/NĐ-CP, responsibility for the administration of the system was overseen by the former **[Ministry of Information and Communications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Information_and_Communications_(Vietnam) "Ministry of Information and Communications (Vietnam)")** ([Vietnamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamese_language "Vietnamese language"): *Bộ Thông tin và Truyền thông*) (**MIC**).[[73]](#cite_note-73)[[74]](#cite_note-74)

#### Current rating system

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Video_game_content_rating_system&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Current rating system")]

Effective 25 December 2024, Article 38 of Decree No. 147/2024/NĐ-CP established a four-tier age classification system for online video games. Publishers are required to self-classify games according to statutory criteria, submit the classification as part of the licensing process, and display the assigned rating on game screens and advertisements.[[75]](#cite_note-75)

* **00+** – Suitable for all ages; limited to animation simulation games without violence, horror, sexual content, or weapon-based combat.
* **12+** – Suitable for players aged 12 and older; permits limited animated combat while prohibiting sexual content and graphic depictions.
* **16+** – Suitable for players aged 16 and older; permits combat but prohibits sexual content and violent imagery.
* **18+** – Suitable for players aged 18 and older; permits more realistic combat depictions but continues to prohibit explicit sexual content.

#### Historical classification

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Video_game_content_rating_system&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Historical classification")]

Prior to 25 December 2024, video games were classified under Article 31a of Decree No. 72/2013/NĐ-CP, as amended by Decree No. 27/2018/NĐ-CP, which established a three-tier age classification system consisting of 00+, 12+, and 18+ categories.[[76]](#cite_note-76)[[77]](#cite_note-77)

* **00+** – Suitable for players of all ages; limited to cartoon simulation games without weapon-based combat, violence, horror elements, or sexual content.
* **12+** – Suitable for players aged 12 and older; permitted limited animated combat while prohibiting sexual content, restricting close-up depictions of weapons, and requiring moderated combat sound effects.
* **18+** – Suitable for adults aged 18 and older; permitted armed combat using weapons but prohibited pornographic activities, sounds, or images.

# ESRB Ratings for Mobile Games: How to Keep Children Safe Online

Anna Lebedinets (soulbodyheal) | 25.09.2025

In today's digital age, mobile games have become a staple in the lives of children and adolescents. With the vast array of games available, understanding ESRB ratings is crucial for parents aiming to ensure their children engage with age-appropriate games. But what is ESRB, and what does ESRB stand for? The ESRB, or Entertainment Software Rating Board, provides a comprehensive ESRB rating chart that helps parents navigate the video game age ratings in North America.

![icon](/assets/static/icon-fb-white.svg)  ![icon](/assets/static/icon-twt-white.svg)

## **Why Age Ratings Are Essential for Video Games**

Age ratings are fundamental in determining the suitability of video game content for different age groups. They offer a standardized way to gauge the maturity required to engage with specific game themes and mechanics, ensuring that children are not exposed to inappropriate content.

### Types of Games That Use Age Ratings

From educational titles for preschoolers to complex strategy games for teenagers, a wide range of games utilize ESRB ratings. These ratings apply to both console and mobile games, making them a universal tool for assessing game content across platforms.

### How Ratings Help Parents Make Informed Choices

By consulting the ESRB rating chart, parents can make informed decisions about which games are safe for their children. This empowers them to select games that align with their family's values and their child's developmental stage.

## **How Parents Can Navigate the World of Mobile Games**

Mobile games require particular attention due to their accessibility and the potential for unsupervised play. Understanding ESRB ratings is the first step in creating a safe and enjoyable gaming environment for children.

### Why Mobile Games Require Age‑Based Controls

Unlike traditional console games, mobile games are easily accessible through smartphones and tablets, often without robust parental controls. Implementing screen time control and utilizing tools like the Kroha app can help manage what children access on their devices.

### Risks Hidden in Popular Kids’ Games

Even games rated for younger audiences can harbor risks such as in‑game purchases, online chat safety concerns, and potential cyberbullying. Recognizing these hidden dangers is essential for effective child online protection.

### The Role of Ratings in Choosing Safe Content

[ESRB ratings](https://www.esrb.org/)provide a clear indication of the content within a game, allowing parents to filter out games that may contain inappropriate elements like violence, language, or sexual themes.

## **What Is the ESRB and How Does It Work**

Understanding what is ESRB is essential for leveraging its ratings effectively. The Entertainment Software Rating Board plays a pivotal role in maintaining the safety and appropriateness of video games in North America.

### A Brief History of the ESRB

Founded in 1994, the ESRB was created in response to concerns about violent content in video games. Since its inception, it has become the standard for video game age ratings North America, ensuring consistent and reliable ratings across all platforms.

### How the Game Rating Process Works

The game classification process involves a detailed review of the game's content by the ESRB rating board. Utilizing tools like the ESRB rating generator, developers submit their games for evaluation, which results in an ESRB rating that reflects the game's suitability for different age groups.

### How the ESRB Differs from PEGI

While the ESRB operates primarily in North America, the PEGI vs ESRB comparison highlights differences in regional rating systems. Understanding these distinctions helps parents who might access games from different parts of the world.

[PEGI (Pan European Game Information)](https://parental-control.net/en/blog/article/pegi-ratings-for-mobile-games-protecting-children-from-harmful-content) is the European video game rating system. The main difference between ESRB and PEGI lies in their geographical application and certain nuances of content classification.

## Understanding ESRB Rating Categories

The ESRB rating categories are designed to provide clear guidelines on the appropriateness of game content for various age groups. Referencing the ESRB rating chart, parents can easily identify the right games for their children.

### E (Everyone) – Suitable for All Ages

ESRB E labels games that are family‑friendly and suitable for players of all ages. These games contain content that is generally inoffensive and appropriate for everyone.

### E10+ (Everyone 10+) – For Children Ages 10 and Up

ESRB E10+ signifies games that are suitable for older children, typically around 10 years old and above. These games may include mild cartoon violence or mild language but remain accessible to younger audiences.

### T (Teen) – For Ages 13 and Up

ESRB T indicates that a game is best suited for teenagers. These games may feature more intense violence, mild profanity, or suggestive themes, making them appropriate for ages 13 and up.

### M (Mature 17+) – For Adults

ESRB M is assigned to games intended for adults due to content that includes intense violence, strong language, or explicit themes. These games are not recommended for players under 17.

### AO (Adults Only 18+) – Strictly for Adults

ESRB AO is the most restrictive category, reserved for games with content suitable only for adults, including graphic violence, sexual content, or other disturbing material.

### RP (Rating Pending) – Awaiting Final Rating

ESRB RP signifies that a game is awaiting its final rating. During this period, parents should exercise caution, as the definitive ESRB rating is yet to be determined.

### RP Likely Mature 17+ (Rating Pending) – rating pending, likely 17+

The final rating has not yet been assigned, but it is expected to be Mature 17+. This designation is used only in advertising, marketing, and promotional materials for video games awaiting a rating and must be replaced with the actual rating once it is determined.

### Content Descriptors – Indicators of Potentially Inappropriate Content

ESRB content descriptors provide additional information about the specific types of content present in a game, such as violence, language, fear, drugs, gambling, sexual themes, or in‑game purchases. These descriptors help parents understand the nuances of a game's content beyond its overall rating.

## **How to Find an ESRB Rating for Mobile Games**

Locating the ESRB rating for mobile games is straightforward. Here's how you can find the rating on popular platforms.

### Where to Locate the Rating in Google Play

In Google Play, the rating is usually located in the app’s description section. Scroll down to the “Additional Information” section to view the age rating and content descriptions.

### How to Check the Age Category in the Apple App Store

In the Apple App Store, the rating is displayed below the app’s name and icon. Additionally, detailed information about the content can be found by tapping “App Privacy” or the “Ratings & Reviews” section.

### What to Look for in a Game Description

When reviewing a game’s description, pay attention to the rating and content descriptions. They provide important information about the game’s suitability for your child’s age and maturity level.

## **Why a Rating Alone Isn’t Enough**

While the ESRB ratings are invaluable, they are not foolproof. Additional considerations are necessary to ensure comprehensive family gaming safety.

### E‑Rated Games May Still Contain Ads

ESRB E rated games might still feature advertisements, some of which may not be suitable for younger audiences. Parents should utilize mobile game content filters to mitigate exposure to inappropriate ads.

### Online Chat and Unwanted Contacts

Many mobile games offer online interactions, posing risks such as online chat safety issues and unwanted contacts. Implementing parental controls and monitoring your child's online interactions is essential to prevent cyberbullying in games and other negative experiences.

### Microtransactions and Gaming Addiction Risks

In‑game purchases can lead to unexpected charges and foster gaming addiction. Setting financial limits and monitoring screen time can help manage these risks effectively.

## **How the Kroha App Helps Parents Manage Mobile Games**

Managing your child's mobile game usage can be challenging, but tools like Kroha, a robust parental control app, simplify this task. Kroha offers features such as block mobile apps, screen time control, and customizable app blocking schedules. These tools empower parents to restrict access to inappropriate games and manage device usage effectively.

### How to Install Kroha on a Smartphone

Installing Kroha is simple:

* Download the Kroha app from the [official website](https://parental-control.net/en/pricing) or your device's app store.
* Follow the on-screen instructions to set up an account.
* Configure the desired settings, including which apps to block and schedule times for device usage.

### App Blocking Features

Kroha provides comprehensive app blocking functionalities to ensure your child's gaming environment is safe and controlled.

#### Full Blocking of Unwanted Games

Parents can fully block specific games or categories of games, preventing access entirely. This feature is particularly useful for excluding games with higher ESRB ratings that may not be suitable for your child.

#### Scheduled Blocking

Kroha allows parents to set scheduled blocking periods, such as during school hours, bedtime, or designated leisure times. This ensures that gaming does not interfere with essential activities and sleep.

## **Creating a Safe Gaming Environment for Your Child**

A safe gaming environment is a blend of tools, communication, and proactive monitoring. Combining ESRB ratings with Kroha parental controls creates a robust defense against potential online hazards.

* **Combining ESRB Ratings with Kroha Parental Controls**

Utilize ESRB ratings to select appropriate games and reinforce these choices with Kroha's blocking and scheduling features. This dual approach ensures that your child accesses safe and suitable content consistently.

* **Regularly Monitoring Games**

Regularly reviewing the games your child plays helps you stay informed about new content and potential changes in game dynamics or ratings.

* **Setting Rules for Device Use**

Establish clear guidelines for when and how devices can be used. Setting boundaries around screen time and gaming can foster healthy habits and prevent overuse.

## Recommended Mobile Games for Children (Based on ESRB Ratings)

Selecting the right games involves understanding their ESRB ratings and ensuring they align with your child's interests and maturity level. Here are some safe and popular options in North America.

### For Preschoolers (ESRB E)

* **PBS Kids Games:** Offers educational and entertaining games tailored for young children, focusing on learning and development.
* **Toca Boca Series:**Creative games that encourage exploration and imaginative play, suitable for all family members.

### For Younger School‑Age Children (ESRB E10+)

* [**Minecraft:**](https://parental-control.net/en/blog/article/how-to-use-minecraft-to-learn-the-basics-of-programming) Promotes creativity and problem-solving through building and exploration in a virtual world.
* **Super Lucky's Tale:** A charming platformer that combines fun gameplay with engaging stories.

### For Teenagers (ESRB T)

* **Fortnite:** A popular battle royale game that encourages strategic thinking and teamwork.
* [**Among Us:**](https://parental-control.net/en/blog/article/is-among-us-safe-for-kids-a-review-for-parents)Enhances social skills and cooperation through multiplayer mystery-solving gameplay.

## Tips for Parents

Ensuring your child's online safety extends beyond understanding ratings. Implementing practical strategies can further protect and guide your child in the digital gaming world.

* **How to Talk to Your Child About the Games They Play**

Maintain open communication about the games your child enjoys. Discussing game content and your family's values fosters trust and awareness.

* **Teaching Your Child to Recognize Risks**

Educate your child on potential online risks, such as interacting with strangers or encountering inappropriate content. Empowering them with knowledge helps them make safer choices.

* **Using Games as a Tool for Learning and Development**

Leverage games that offer educational value, promoting cognitive and social development, while keeping your child engaged and entertained.

## Conclusion

While ESRB ratings serve as a reliable tool for assessing game suitability, they are not a complete safeguard. Complementing ratings with practical solutions like Kroha enhances daily monitoring and ensures a comprehensive approach to safe gaming. Achieving a secure gaming environment is a collective effort involving attentive parenting, ongoing dialogue, and the strategic use of technology.

### ¡Vamos a Jugar!

Las clasificaciones de ESRB facilitan que los padres estén informados sobre los videojuegos que juegan sus hijos, pero hay más cosas que los padres pueden hacer para mantenerse involucrados y actualizados.

[→](https://www.esrb.org/vamos-a-jugar/)

[←](#) [→](#)

## ESRB Blog

### [A Parent’s Guide to Star Wars: Galactic Racer](https://www.esrb.org/blog/a-parents-guide-to-star-wars-galactic-racer/)

Star Wars: Galactic Racer at a Glance Star Wars: Galactic Racer is rated E10+ for Everyone 10+ Players will race with a variety of in-universe vehicles like Podracers, speeders, and more Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fast-paced, run-based racing game Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a marriage of one of my favorite science fiction […]

[Read the Full Story](https://www.esrb.org/blog/a-parents-guide-to-star-wars-galactic-racer/)

[View All](https://www.esrb.org/blog/)

### Did You Know?

65% of the ESRB ratings assigned to physical and console downloadable video games in 2024 were either E (Everyone) or E10+ (Everyone 10+).

 [Learn More on our Blog](https://www.esrb.org/blog/e-for-everyone-was-assigned-most-often-in-2024/)

### Did You Know?

83% of parents with kids who play video games are aware of ESRB ratings and 77% regularly check them before buying a game. (Source: Hart Research Associates, 2025)

 [Learn More on our Blog](https://www.esrb.org/blog/research-no-news-is-good-news-when-it-comes-to-appropriate-video-games/)

### Did You Know?

Most parents consider each part (Rating Category, Content Descriptors, Interactive Elements) of the ESRB rating system to be either “very” or “extremely” important when deciding if a game or app is appropriate for their kids. (Source: Hart Research Associates, 2025)

 [Learn More on Ratings Guide](https://www.esrb.org/ratings-guide/)

### Did You Know?

Industry guidelines, which are enforced by the ESRB, prohibit the inappropriate target marketing of Mature-rated games.

 [Learn More about Principles and Guidelines](https://www.esrb.org/ratings/principles-guidelines/)

### Did You Know?

ESRB has an enforcement system which allows for the imposition of sanctions, fines (including fines up to $1 million), and corrective actions on publishers for non-compliance with its guidelines.

 [Learn More about Rating Process](https://www.esrb.org/ratings/ratings-process/)

### Did You Know?

According to the U.S. [Federal Trade Commission](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/press-releases/2013/03/ftc-undercover-shopper-survey-entertainment-ratings-enforcement) 87% of kids under the age of 17 are turned away when trying to buy an M-rated game at retail.

 [Learn More on our Blog](https://www.esrb.org/blog/federal-trade-commission-finds-that-esrb-has-most-effective-ratings-enforcement/)

### Did You Know?

The late U.S. Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia wrote: “This [ESRB rating] system does much to ensure that minors cannot purchase seriously violent games on their own, and that parents who care about the matter can readily evaluate the games their children bring home.”

 [Learn More at supremecourt.gov](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/10pdf/08-1448.pdf)

### Did You Know?

The E (Everyone) rating was originally called K-A (Kids to Adults) but was changed in 1998.

 [Learn More in History of ESRB](https://www.esrb.org/history/)

### Did You Know?

The ESRB rating system has three parts – Rating Categories, Content Descriptors and Interactive Elements, the latter of which were introduced in 2013.

 [Learn More on Ratings Guide](https://www.esrb.org/ratings-guide/)

### Did You Know?

Introduced in 2008, Rating Summaries provide greater detail about the content in physical games rated by the ESRB, and are exclusively available on this website or the ESRB mobile app by conducting a title search.

 [Learn More on Ratings Guide](https://www.esrb.org/ratings-guide/)

### Did You Know?

ESRB uses more than 30 different Content Descriptors to help communicate what’s in a game.

 [Learn More on Ratings Guide](https://www.esrb.org/ratings-guide/)

### Did You Know?

The FTC considers the ESRB to have “the strongest self-regulatory code” among media rating systems in the U.S. and has confirmed that retailers maintain a high store policy compliance rate.

 [Learn More on our Blog](https://www.esrb.org/blog/federal-trade-commission-finds-that-esrb-has-most-effective-ratings-enforcement/)

### Did You Know?

Founded in 2013 by many of the world’s leading video game rating authorities, the International Age Rating Coalition (IARC) administers the first globally streamlined age classification process for digital games and mobile apps that respects the unique cultural norms of each region.

 [Learn More at globalratings.com](https://www.globalratings.com/)

### Did You Know?

In 1999 ESRB Privacy Online (now called ESRB Privacy Certified) launched its certification program and was sanctioned by the FTC as a “Safe Harbor” under [Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act](https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/rules/rulemaking-regulatory-reform-proceedings/childrens-online-privacy-protection-rule) (COPPA).

 [Learn More on privacy](https://www.esrb.org/privacy/)

### Did You Know?

More than 67% of parents would be more comfortable allowing their children to download and play a game certified by ESRB Privacy Certified (Source: Hart Research Associates, 2024).

 [Learn More on privacy](https://www.esrb.org/privacy/)

### Did You Know?

It’s never too late to have “the conversation” with your kids about what, when, and how they can play!

 [Learn More on Family gaming guide](https://www.esrb.org/tools-for-parents/family-gaming-guide/)

### Did You Know?

Activating parental controls on your children’s video game devices helps you enforce house rules, such as limiting play time, blocking games with certain ESRB ratings, and managing in-game spending.

 [Learn More on Parental controls](https://www.esrb.org/tools-for-parents/parental-controls/)

### Did You Know?

The average gamer is 36 years old.

 [Learn More at theesa.com](https://www.theesa.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/2025-Essential-Facts-Booklet-05-30-25-RGB.pdf)

# About Age Ratings

Games available on Nintendo Switch will have one of the following age-appropriate rating icons displayed on them. This is decided by an industry ratings board. Please use these ratings to help you ensure your children stay safe as they play on the Nintendo Switch console.

A variety of expressions are present in games, but you can set what games your child may play, in accordance with ESRB and PEGI age ratings.

![NINTENDO SWITCH™️ Parental Controls](./img/common/parental-controls.svg)

## ESRB Rating

The Entertainment Games Rating Board (ESRB) used in the United States and Canada is comprised of three parts: rating category, content descriptors, and interactive elements.

### Rating Categories

The rating category is indicated on the front of the games's packaging and suggests the suitable ages for a title.

![Front of Packaging](./img/ratings/img01.jpg)
![Everyone (E): For all ages](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/E.svg)

Everyone (E):   
For all ages

![Everyone 10+ (E10+): Ages 10 years and up](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/E10plus.svg)

Everyone 10+ (E10+):   
Ages 10 years and up

![Teen (T): Ages 13 years and up](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/T.svg)

Teen (T):   
Ages 13 years and up

![Mature (M): Ages 17 years and up](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/M.svg)

Mature (M):   
Ages 17 years and up

![Adult only 18+: Ages 18 years and up](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/AO.svg)

Adult only 18+:   
Ages 18 years and up

### Content Descriptors

The content descriptors can be found on the back of the packaging, and indicate the wording on which the age category has been determined.

![Back of Packaging](./img/ratings/img02.jpg)

Alcohol Reference

Animated Blood

Cartoon Violence

Comic Mischief

Fantasy Violence

Crude Humor

Language

Use of Tobacco

### Interactive Elements

Interactive elements highlight interactive or online features, such as whether there is user interaction. There may be descriptions for functions not available in your region.

![Back of Packaging](./img/ratings/img03.jpg)

In-Game Purchases

In-Game Purchases (Includes Random Items)

Users Interact

Shares Location

Unrestricted Internet

You can also check the rating category, content descriptor and interactive elements on a games's page.

## PEGI Ratings

PEGI (Pan European Game Information) age rating system rates titles and is used in European countries. It is made up of a rating category and content descriptor icon.

### Rating Categories

The rating category is indicated on the front of the games's packaging and suggests the suitable ages for a title.

![Front of Packaging](./img/ratings/img04.jpg)
![For ages 3+](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/pegi3.png)

For ages 3+

![For ages 7+](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/pegi7.png)

For ages 7+

![For ages 12+](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/pegi12.png)

For ages 12+

![For ages 16+](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/pegi16.png)

For ages 16+

![For ages 18+](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/pegi18.png)

For ages 18+

You can also check the rating category, content descriptor and interactive elements on a games's page.

## IMDA Ratings

The IMDA game rating adopted in Singapore consists of rating categories and Consumer Advice.

### Rating Categories

The IMDA rating category is indicated on the games's packaging and suggests the suitable ages for a title.

![Front of Packaging](./img/ratings/img06.jpg)
![For all ages](./img/ratings/no-icon.png)

For all ages

![Unsuitable for Persons Under 16](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/imda16_b.png)

Unsuitable for Persons Under 16

![Restricted to Persons Aged 18 and Above](../../../../common-a/games/img/rating/imda18_b.png)

Restricted to Persons Aged 18 and Above

### Consumer Advice

Consumer advice highlights the major content concerns found in the title, such as violence, nudity, and scenes of a sexual nature.

![Front of Packaging](./img/ratings/img07.jpg)

You can check the rating category and Consumer Advice for a title on each games's page (only for ADV16 and M18 games).
